alerts.title: Weight Gain on DTG Regimen
alerts.message: Guidelines state the possibility of weight gain should be discussed when starting all ART regimens, as obesity is an increasing problem in HIV care. The patient has gained 17 kg (BMI increased from 25.6 to 32.4 kg/m²) over 18 months since switching to TLD (TDF/3TC/DTG). She also reports fatigue. Acanthosis nigricans suggests insulin resistance. While DTG-containing regimens are associated with weight gain, non-drug contributors like diet, exercise, and family history of diabetes should also be considered.

evidence.recommended_action: Discuss weight gain risk, provide proactive advice on diet and exercise, and monitor for metabolic complications.

alerts.title: New Metabolic Syndrome
alerts.message: Patient has developed multiple components of metabolic syndrome since ART switch: impaired fasting glucose (118 mg/dL), pre-diabetic HbA1c (6.1%), dyslipidemia (LDL 148 mg/dL, TG 212 mg/dL), elevated BP (138/88 mmHg), and central obesity (waist 96 cm). Acanthosis nigricans is a cutaneous marker of insulin resistance. This cluster increases cardiovascular risk. Weight gain on DTG may be a contributing factor, but family history of type 2 diabetes is also relevant.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess and manage cardiovascular risk factors. Consider lifestyle intervention and monitor glucose per DTG transition guidelines.

alerts.title: Missing Glucose Monitoring Plan
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year for people living with HIV transitioned to DTG. The patient switched to TLD (DTG-based) 18 months ago. While she now has impaired fasting glucose and pre-diabetes, there is no documented plan for ongoing glycemic monitoring or management in the clinician's assessment.

evidence.recommended_action: Implement guideline-recommended glucose monitoring every 3 months and document a management plan for pre-diabetes.
